findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category setting has no matching category
findings.body: The migration executes `SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'` and indexes `[0]['id'].to_i` on the result. On any installation where either the `embed_category` site_setting row does not exist (e.g. fresh installs, upgrades from setups that never set it, or sites whose value was reset/cleared) or where the value does not match any category name, the result set is empty, `[0]` returns nil, and `nil['id'].to_i` raises NoMethodError and aborts the migration. The migration needs a nil guard (and the same applies if the SQL ever returns zero rows): e.g. `rows = execute(...); category_id = rows && rows.first ? rows.first['id'].to_i : SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`.

findings.title: Raw SQL string interpolation of host value in migration
findings.body: The migration inserts each host with `execute "INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`. The value `h` comes straight from the prior `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` admin setting. If that value ever contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters) the migration's SQL is malformed or, in the worst case, executes unintended statements. Even though the value is admin-controlled and only used at migration time, this should be parameterized (or assigned through the EmbeddableHost model with `.create!`) so a stray quote can't break the upgrade and so the migration is robust to any prior state of the data.

findings.title: update/destroy actions crash when EmbeddableHost is not found
findings.body: `update` does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` then passes `host` directly to `save_host`, which immediately invokes `host.host = …`. If the id does not match a record, `host` is nil and this raises NoMethodError (and renders a 500). `destroy` has the same problem: it calls `host.destroy` on a nil record. The controller should detect the missing record and return `not_found` (or render an error JSON), matching the convention used by the rest of `Admin::*Controller`s.

findings.title: before_validation callback crashes when host is nil
findings.body: `before_validation` runs `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. If a record is created without a `host` attribute (e.g. mass-assignment that omits host, or any path that calls `valid?`/`save` on an instance whose host is nil), `nil.sub!` raises NoMethodError and validation aborts before any user-friendly error is shown. The callback should no-op when host is blank, e.g. return unless host.present? (and ideally the controller already enforces this, but the model should defend itself).

findings.title: Plural hydration retains undefined entries when IDs do not resolve
findings.body: In `_hydrateEmbedded` the plural branch sets `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || [];`. When `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for an id (for example an `embeddable_host_ids` value that has no matching record in the side-loaded `embeddable_hosts` array, the lookup returns nothing), `.map` still produces an array containing undefined entries. The `hydrated || []` fallback never fires because the array is non-empty, so the resulting model attribute contains `undefined` values. Any subsequent UI iteration (`{{#each}}`, `.length`, `.get('id')`) will then either render blank rows or throw. The fallback should filter falsy entries, e.g. `(hydrated || []).compact`, before assignment.
